label: Maps and directions
description: Where the Maps window gets its map, its search and its turn-by-turn directions. With no key at all it uses free OpenStreetMap services (kept to their usage rules: one request a second, Dayspring's own name on every request, answers cached). A Google Maps key switches to Google automatically. Every one of them needs the internet; the voice commands themselves are understood offline.

entries.model: Maps Platform (Maps Embed, Places API (New), Routes API)
entries.notes: Needs a Google Cloud project with billing turned on and an API key. The map (Maps Embed API) is free with no limit. Search (Places Text Search) has 5,000 free requests a month, or 1,000 when ratings and opening hours are turned on; directions (Routes, traffic-unaware) have 10,000 free a month, 5,000 with live traffic. Set daily quotas so a mistake can't cost money.
howToSetUp: In the Google Cloud console, open your project (or make one) and turn on billing.
APIs & Services → Library: enable Maps Embed API, Places API (New) and Routes API.
APIs & Services → Credentials → Create credentials → API key. Under API restrictions, allow only those three APIs.
For each of the three APIs, open Quotas and set a small daily limit (for example 100 requests a day). Add a budget alert under Billing.
In Dayspring, Settings → Maps: paste the key, press Save key, then Test.

entries.notes: Free, no key. Used for searches you finish (Enter, or by voice), never for suggestions while typing, as its usage policy asks. At most one request a second. Checked live once against a real town search.
howToSetUp: Nothing to set up: it's the default when there's no Google key.

entries.notes: Free, no key, OpenStreetMap data. Asked at most once a second, after you stop typing for a moment.

Free, no key: the routing servers openstreetmap.org itself uses. One request a second, fair use only. No transit. Avoiding highways or tolls is tried and said plainly when it isn't possible. Checked live once with a short drive between two addresses.
howToSetUp: Nothing to set up: used when there's no Google key and no OpenRouteService key.

entries.notes: A free key gives 2,000 routes a day. When it's saved it's used before the FOSSGIS servers; if it fails, those take over.
howToSetUp: Sign up at openrouteservice.org and copy your API key from the dashboard.
Settings → Maps: paste it under OpenRouteService, Save key, then Test.

entries.notes: For light personal use, as the tile policy allows. Dayspring fetches the pictures itself with its own name, keeps them for a week, asks for at most two at a time, and always shows the © OpenStreetMap credit.
Use the QR code or Send to phone: Google Maps links open on an iPhone too.
entries.reason: Apple Maps' web service needs a paid Apple Developer account and signed tokens, and has no way to hand turn-by-turn steps to another app on Windows.

entries.notes: Send the trip to your phone and open it in Waze from there if you prefer it.
entries.reason: Waze has no public routing or search service for other apps.
